title: Parts VII and VIII (ownership and views; classes, shared owners, links)

found.group: G3: Parts VII and VIII (ownership and views; classes, shared owners, links)

findings.title: Proof (1) of [WK-7] is circular: a fresh holder passes its own test, so the loop [WK-6] refuses is accepted
findings.program:
class Node:
    next: Option[shares mut Node] = None

fn make_pair():
    a = shares mut Node()
    b = shares mut Node()
    a.next = Some(shares mut b)      # (2): holder `a` fresh, no owner of it stored yet: closes none (true)
    b.next = Some(shares mut a)      # <- closes a -> b -> a. Proof (1) for the stored value `a`: made here; the one owner stored into it since, `shares mut b`, names `b`, which "itself meets (1)" (made here, and at this moment no owner has been stored into `b`). So the line "closes none": accepted; neither node is ever freed
findings.why: [WK-7]: "(1) the stored value was made in this function, on the line or earlier, and since then no owner has been stored into it or into anything it owns but values that themselves meet (1)". The recursion is judged at the line, where the holder is itself a fresh value into which nothing has been stored yet, so the holder always meets (1) and a loop closed between two fresh objects is never seen. [WK-6] says of this very program "refused: nothing opens the loop", so the two rules disagree, and the one an implementer builds from (the exact test of [WK-7], "every implementation applies exactly these") accepts it. Also unsaid: whether an owner given at the value's making (`Node(next=Some(shares mut a))`) counts as "stored since then".
findings.proposed_text: Replace in [WK-7] the sentence "(1) the stored value was made in this function, on the line or earlier, and since then no owner has been stored into it or into anything it owns but values that themselves meet (1)" with: "(1) the stored value reaches the holder through no owner: it was made in this function, on the line or earlier, and every owner stored into it or into anything it owns, at its making (a constructor argument) or since, names a value that meets this same test and is neither the object the place belongs to nor an owner of that object, directly or through other owners (`root.children.push(shares mut child)` with `child = shares mut Node(...)` made above it and given no owner: a tree built from the top down closes nothing; `b.next = Some(shares mut a)` after `a.next = Some(shares mut b)` fails it, since `a` owns `b`, the holder)".
findings.codes: E3032 reused (shape B17); no new code

findings.title: The graph of owners misses plain-owned edges, and a store judged in a library closes a loop a dependant makes (extends O1)
findings.program:
# one package: a plain field is not an edge of [WK-5]'s list
class Inner:
    back: Option[shares mut Outer] = None
class Outer:
    inner: Inner = Inner()
fn main():
    o = shares mut Outer()
    o.inner.back = Some(shares mut o)     # <- `shares mut Outer` reaches `Inner` only through `Outer.inner`, a one-owner class field, which [WK-5] does not list as an owner edge: "closes none"; `o` is never freed

# two packages: the store is in `lib`, compiled with no `Back`
# lib
pub interface Plugin:
    fn run()
pub class Host:
    plugins: Array[owns dyn Plugin] = []
    fn add(owns p: owns dyn Plugin):
        this.plugins.push(owns p)        # lib's graph: `dyn Plugin` reaches no `Host`: closes none
# app
import lib
class Back(lib.Plugin):
    host: shares mut lib.Host
    fn run(): pass
fn main():
    h = shares mut lib.Host()
    b = Back(host=shares mut h)          # (2): `b` is fresh and nothing owns it: closes none (true)
    h.add(owns b)                        # <- closes h -> b -> h; the only store is lib's line, judged once; nothing refuses; `h` and `b` leak
findings.why: [WK-5]: the owner edges are "a field holding a `shares`, `shares mut` or `thread_shared` value, or a collection of them; a function value's state ...; a channel end ...; a `Retained[ForeignCallback]` token": a plain field, an `owns T`, an inline struct or an enum payload that in turn holds a shared owner is not an edge, so the reach test of [WK-7] ("the stored value's type can reach the holder's type through owner edges") fails to see `Outer -> Inner`. [WK-5] also says the graph is built "over the whole program" and a function value's state "from every function the program can put there", which a package compiled once cannot see ([BLD-1], [EFF-4]); [WK-7] judges "a store of an owner ... into a place of an object" at the line of the store, which is in the library. A `dyn I` place has no edge at all in the list. [WK-15]: "In Safe Ember nothing leaks through a loop of owners" is then false. AUDIT O1 lists [OBJ-1], [THR-2], [WK-18] as the whole-program facts; [WK-5]/[WK-7] are the same shape and are not listed.
findings.proposed_text: Add to [WK-5]: "An owner edge also runs through every place a type owns alone (a plain field or element, an `owns T`, a struct or enum payload stored inline) to the type held there, since what a value owns alone reaches what that owns; a `dyn I`, `owns dyn I`, `shares dyn I` or base-class place has the edges of every kind the program can put there, and a function value's state those of every function ([EFF-1])." Add to [WK-7] after "every implementation applies exactly these (XVIII.4)": "A store whose stored value, or whose holder, is a parameter or `this` is not judged in the body: the function's summary records that it stores that parameter into a place of that other parameter or of `this` (in the package's interface file across a package's edge, [EFF-4]), and each call of the function is the store, judged there by the two proofs with the argument as the stored value and the other argument, or the object, as the holder. A call through a function value, or through a `dyn`, interface or `virtual` method, counts as storing every owner it is given into the value or object it is called on, unless every function the program can put there is seen ([EFF-4]). So every store is judged in the package that can see both the stored value and the holder, with the edges of the types it can see, and a loop a dependant closes through a library's method is refused at the dependant's call (`h.add(owns b)`: \"this closes a loop of owners (`h` → `b` → `h`): `add` stores `b` in `h.plugins`, and `b.host` owns `h`; make the link back `weakref`: `host: weakref lib.Host`\")."
findings.codes: E3032 reused; the interface file gains one recorded fact per function (which parameter it stores into which)

findings.title: `copy of` (a `Clone`) gives a parent link a target outside [WK-17]'s pattern, and the proved test-free read then reads an ended parent
findings.why: [WK-17] condition 1 enumerates the lines that give the field a target as "every line that gives the field a target, `x.parent = weakref o`, is followed in the same function ... by a line that puts `x` into a place `o` owns alone", and the implementer checks that pattern; but [OWN-8] says a value that holds links "is copied field by field ... each link is copied as a link to the same target", so `copy of` gives `twin.parent` a target with no placing line, and so do `mem.swap`/`mem.replace` on the field or on an object holding it. The proof "an object's parent owns it, so while the object lives its parent lives" is then false for the copy, and [WK-17] compiles the read with no header test.
findings.proposed_text: Add to [WK-17] condition 1, after "(`c.parent = None`)": "the field is given a target by nothing else: not by a `copy of` of an object of the class, whose `Clone` copies the link ([OWN-8]), so a class of the family that has or derives `Clone` fails the condition; not by `mem.swap`, `mem.replace` or `mem.take` on the field or on an object that holds it; and a constructor argument that gives it a target counts as such a line, which the placing line must follow".
findings.codes: none: condition 1 fails and every read tests, as the rule already says for that case

findings.title: A `drop` in a derived class (or in a value the node owns) reads a parent link test-free while the parent is being ended
findings.why: [WK-17] condition 1: "the objects have one owner ... and their class has no `drop` method of its own" names one class, where the places hold objects of every class of the family; condition 2 speaks of "the point where the object whose link is read is known to live (a view of it)", which inside a `drop` is the ended object itself ([WK-3]: an object is ended before its `drop` runs, and a child's `drop` opening `this.parent` while the parent is being ended "finds it ended"), a finding only the header test makes. An owned value with a `drop` that reads the link (a struct field holding `weakref Node`) is the same hole.
findings.proposed_text: In [WK-17] condition 1 replace "and their class has no `drop` method of its own" with "no class of the family, and no type of a value such an object owns, has a `drop` of its own". Add to condition 2: "A read inside a `drop`, or inside a function a `drop` may call ([EFF-1]), is never proved: the object whose link is read is being ended, and its parent may be ending with it ([WK-3]); such a read tests."
findings.codes: none: the read tests, as [WK-17] says where a condition fails

findings.title: After the making thread ends, a subtract that finds the queue closed ends the value while home-counted owners still hold it
findings.program:
class Big:
    fn drop(): println("gone")
class Box:
    v: thread_shared Big

fn main():
    (tx, rx) = channel()
    maker = spawn(fn() owns tx:
        big = thread_shared Big()            # home = 1
        x = Box(v=thread_shared big)         # home = 2 (plain adds, [RC-4] point 1)
        y = Box(v=thread_shared big)         # home = 3
        mem.drop(owns big)                   # home = 2
        tx.send(owns x)                      # x handed over; `big` travels inside it (point 5): home stays 2, away 0
        tx.send(owns y))                     # the maker ends: its queue is emptied and closed
    maker.join()
    x = rx.recv()
    mem.drop(owns x)                         # <- away = -1 < 0, the queue is closed: "a subtract that finds the queue closed ends the value itself": Big's drop runs, its block is freed
    y = rx.recv()
    println(y.v is not None)                 # reads a freed Big; ending `y` ends it a second time
findings.why: [RC-4] point 3: "A value whose making thread has ended is ended at once by the thread that ends its last owner: a thread's end empties and closes its queue in one atomic step, and a subtract that finds the queue closed ends the value itself". The subtract that finds the queue closed is any subtract that takes the away count below zero (point 2), which happens while the home count is still positive whenever more than one home-counted owner travelled inside other objects; "its last owner" is asserted, not tested. Point 1: "Only the making thread reads both", so the ending thread, read literally, cannot test the sum either. Verdict 101 says "the other thread deletes it at once if the making thread has ended" with "The object has A + B owners"; the text drops the A + B test.
findings.proposed_text: In [RC-4] point 3 replace "and a subtract that finds the queue closed ends the value itself, so no value waits for a thread that is gone" with: "and a subtract that finds the queue closed reads the home count, which no thread changes once the making thread has ended (the close is a release and the subtract that finds it an acquire, [RT-8]), and ends the value only when the home count and the away count the subtract returned add up to zero; so no value waits for a thread that is gone, and none ends while an owner the making thread counted still holds it".
findings.codes: none (runtime); [RT-8]'s orders gain the close/subtract pair

findings.title: [RC-4]'s unsaid transitions: home reaching zero with away owners, the state after a queue merge, the end as one atomic step, and the making thread's test of the handed-over mark
findings.program:
Implementer question: what does the making thread do when its home count reaches zero and the away count is positive? Program that forces it:

fn main():
    log = thread_shared Log()                # home = 1
    t = spawn(fn() thread_shared log: ...)   # the capture hands it over (point 4): home 0, away 1, marked handed over: fine
    # but with `thread_shared` owners that travel inside a channel's `Box` (point 5) and no hand-over of `log` itself:
    x = Box(v=thread_shared log)             # home = 2
    tx.send(owns x)                          # home 2, away 0, not handed over
    mem.drop(owns log)                       # home = 1; the maker holds nothing it can see
    # worker: x = rx.recv(); mem.drop(owns x)  -> away = -1: queued; maker's check point: home 1 + away -1 = 0: ends. Right.
    # now the worker instead makes an owner first: w = thread_shared x.v (away 1), then ends x (away 0, not below zero: nothing queued),
    # then ends w (away -1: queued). The maker at its check point: home 1 + away -1 = 0: ends. Right.
    # but with two workers each holding one away owner when home reaches 0 by the maker's own `mem.drop(owns log)` BEFORE the send:
    # home 0, away 2; the last worker's end: away 1 -> 0, not below zero, nothing queues, the maker's home is already 0 and it reads nothing: `log` is never ended (its drop never runs)
findings.why: Point 1 says "The value lives while the two add up to more than zero. Only the making thread reads both" and point 2 queues only when "the away count goes below zero"; nothing says what the making thread does when its own subtract takes the home count to zero while the away count is positive (it must mark the value handed over, so that the away count's reaching zero ends it, as point 4's "a later end on another thread never goes through the queue" needs). Point 2's merge, "it adds each value's home count into its away count, and ends the value when the sum is zero", says nothing about the state when the sum is not zero (home must become zero, the queued mark cleared and the handed-over mark set, else the next below-zero subtract on another thread finds the value already marked queued and nothing enqueues it again: a leak) nor that the end is a compare-exchange on the away word that sets the ended mark only if no opening of a `weakref` link ([WK-12]: an atomic add on another thread, "undone when the value is marked ended") came between the read and the mark (else the view's count is added to a value the maker is ending). Point 4 says "from then on every thread, the making thread included, counts in the away count", which means every count operation on the making thread first tests the mark (one load and one branch per operation, not the "plain adds and subtracts" of point 1), and a view opened as a home count ([RC-5] point 2) must be undone on the away count if the value was handed over meanwhile; neither the test nor its cost row (§X.4) is said. Point 4's list of places ("a lock-guarded `thread_shared` container") also leaves a `guarded by` field holding `Option[thread_shared T]`, and the making of a `thread_shared fn()` value that a library may spawn, to the implementer.
findings.proposed_text: Add to [RC-4]: "1a. **Home reaching zero.** When the making thread's subtract takes the home count to zero and the away count is positive, it marks the value handed over in one atomic step on the away word (point 4): from then on every owner is counted away, and the subtract that takes the away count to zero ends the value. When both are zero it ends the value itself." In point 2 after "ends the value when the sum is zero" add: "; when the sum is positive it moves the home count into the away count in one atomic step that also clears the queued mark and sets the handed-over mark, so that the value is counted away from then on and a later subtract below zero never finds a stale queued mark." Add: "2a. **The end is one atomic step.** Whichever thread ends a `thread_shared` value sets the ended mark with a compare-exchange on the away word that succeeds only if the count is what it read; a `weakref` opening that added to the away count meanwhile makes it fail, and the thread reads again." In point 4 replace "into a lock-guarded `thread_shared` container, through a channel, into the capture of a thread it spawns or of a callback C keeps" with "into any place reachable from a `thread_shared` value (a `guarded by` field or container under its lock), through a channel, into the state of a `thread_shared fn()` value when it is made ([CLO-16]), or into the token of a callback C keeps", and add: "On the making thread every count operation on a `thread_shared` value first tests the handed-over mark, one load and one branch (§X.4), and a view's count opened on the home count ([RC-5] point 2) is undone on the count the mark names at the view's end."
findings.codes: none (runtime); §X.4 gains a row: the mark test per count operation on the making thread

findings.title: "A value with one owner is not counted" leaves unsaid what the header's count holds, which the `weakref` test reads
findings.why: [RC-1]: "A value with one owner is not counted: its owner ends it"; [RT-10]: "an object with one owner is never counted" and "The subtract that reaches zero marks the object ended before its `drop` runs", but a one-owner object has no subtract; [WK-12]/[WK-2]/[WK-3] say an opened link "finds it ended" and [OBJ-3] that "the weak count starts at 1 on behalf of all owners" without saying what the owner count of a one-owner object holds while it lives or at its end. [RC-1]'s local case ("a value that is not a class object is then made in a block of its own from the line that made it") also names "the line that made it", which for `xs = make()` is in another function; the line meant is the one that declares the local.
findings.proposed_text: In [RC-1] replace "A value with one owner is not counted: its owner ends it." with: "A value with one owner is not counted: no owner is added or subtracted, and its owner ends it. Where a `weakref` link may reach it ([OBJ-1]) its header's count is written twice: 1 at its making and 0 at its end, before its `drop` runs, so that opening a link tests one number ([WK-12]: the target lives while its count is not zero); where none may, the count is never written." Replace "from the line that made it" with "from the line that declares the local (`xs = make()` puts the result in that block)".
findings.milestone: M6b (the header), M4 (shares of a local)

findings.title: [RC-1] allows `thread_shared` of a local that owns its value; [OWN-13] refuses it with E7017
findings.program:
class Names:
    items: Array[String] = []

fn share_and_keep():
    names = Names()
    names.items.push(owns String("a"))
    t = spawn(fn() thread_shared names: println(names.items.len()))   # <- [RC-1]: `names` is "a local of this function that owns its value", so `thread_shared names` is legal and the local's type is `thread_shared Names` throughout; [OWN-13]: E7017, "create it shared: `names = thread_shared Names()`"
    t.join()
findings.why: [RC-1]: "`shares x`, `shares mut x` and `thread_shared x` are written before a new value, a local of this function that owns its value (which becomes one of the owners ... and the local's type is the shared type throughout the function) or a name that is already such an owner". [OWN-13]: "`thread_shared x`, one more owner on any thread, written only before a new value (`names = thread_shared Names()`) or a value already `thread_shared` (`E7017` otherwise ...)". A compiler must pick one; the 32-byte header and the chunk record of [OBJ-1]/[RC-4] favour [OWN-13] (the making line must already know), and [RC-1]'s "throughout the function" would make a one-thread local's every count operation atomic on a path the programmer never wrote.
findings.proposed_text: In [RC-1] replace "`shares x`, `shares mut x` and `thread_shared x` are written before a new value, a local of this function that owns its value (...) or a name that is already such an owner" with: "`shares x` and `shares mut x` are written before a new value, a local of this function that owns its value (which becomes one of the owners: ... the local's type is the shared type throughout the function) or a name that is already such an owner; `thread_shared x` is written only before a new value or a name that is already a `thread_shared` owner (`E7017`, [OWN-13]): its header and its making thread's record are written where the value is made, and a local made one-thread is not remade for another thread."

findings.title: A view a call returns into a `static mut` has the static region and no source parameter, so the caller keeps nothing viewed
findings.program:
static mut LOG: Array[String] = [String("first")]

fn head() -> StrView:
    return LOG[0]            # [LT-3]: a static item's view has the static region, "which outlives everything"; no source parameter, so [LT-1] rules 2 and 3 tie the result to nothing

fn main():
    s = head()
    LOG.clear()              # <- [BRW-17] ends a view a call gave "at any change that may reshape what it points into", but what `s` points into is recorded nowhere: [LT-22]'s summary says "which part of the result points into which parameter"
    println(s)               # reads the freed text of the first string
findings.why: [LT-3]: "String literals, `bytes` literals, `static` items and views of them have the `static` region, which outlives everything"; [STA-1] makes `static mut NAME` "a module variable that may change" whose functions "may grow or free" it ([STA-3]). [LT-1]: "A call's result that is a view ... point[s] into the arguments they may come from" and [LT-22]: the summary records "which part of the result points into which parameter"; a module variable is no parameter, so the caller cannot apply [BRW-17] to it. [BRW-21] shows the compiler knows `LOG[0]` is part of `LOG` in the caller's own lines, but not through a call's result. [BRW-16] also leaves unsaid whether `LOG[0]` in a function is a position (its list of what a position's list is reached through does not name a module variable).
findings.proposed_text: Replace [LT-3] with: "* `[LT-3]` String literals, `bytes` literals, `static` items (which never change, [STA-1]) and views of them have the `static` region, which outlives everything. A `static mut` is a place with one owner, the program, reached by each function that names it as a local of that function is ([BRW-16]: `LOG[0]` is a position; [BRW-17] for a view into its contents): a result that points into one is recorded in the function's summary as pointing into that variable, beside the parameters ([LT-22], [EFF-4]), and a caller keeps it viewed as it keeps an argument, so a reshape of it while the result lives is `E3060` at the later use (\"`LOG.clear()` (line 7) may free the text `s` views (`head()` returns a view of `LOG`, its line 4), and `s` is used on line 8; keep your own copy: `s = String(head())`\") and a change `E3021`."
findings.codes: E3060, E3021 reused; the summary of [LT-22] gains the module variables a result may point into
findings.milestone: M2 (`static mut` as a place), M6a

findings.title: The per-kind check of a call through `dyn` is a whole-program fact: a library's function compiled before a dependant's kind existed is not re-checked at the dependant's call (extends O1)
findings.program:
# lib, compiled with `Mine` only
pub interface Picker:
    fn pick(other: Array[int]) -> Span[int]
pub class Mine(Picker):
    items: Array[int]
    fn pick(other: Array[int]) -> Span[int]: return this.items
pub fn show(p: dyn Picker, ref mut xs: Array[int]):
    r = p.pick(xs)
    xs.push(owns 3)          # accepted: every kind the library sees returns a view of `this`
    println(r)
# app
import lib
class Yours(lib.Picker):
    fn pick(other: Array[int]) -> Span[int]: return other
fn main():
    xs = [9]
    lib.show(Yours(), ref mut xs)   # <- [LT-1] says this is refused "at `xs.push(owns 3)` for `show(Yours(...))`", a line of `lib`, with a fact the app's compiler has only if the interface file carries it; it does not, so the call compiles: `r` views the buffer `push` moved
findings.why: [LT-1]: "A `dyn` or `virtual` method's call is decided by the code of each kind that may reach it, the types the program gives to the function, followed through its names and calls ... and is refused at `xs.push(owns 3)` for `show(Yours(items=[9]))`" and [BRW-21] works a function's fact out "through a function value, or through an interface, `dyn` or virtual method, by every function the program can put there" and "keeps that fact with the function (in the package's interface file across a package's edge, [EFF-4])": the fact kept is one verdict, made when the library was compiled, with the kinds it could see. [LT-48] shows the shape of the missing record (one bit per source parameter in the kind's table) but only for `runtime`. Verdict 151 ("checked for each kind the function is given") is kept by the proposal, which makes the check possible from another package; the fallback of E0901 would refuse every `pub` function with a `dyn` parameter.
findings.proposed_text: Add to [LT-1] after "unless the parameter says `runtime` ([LT-48])": "Across a package's edge the kinds are the caller's to give, so the package's interface file records, for each `pub` function and each `dyn`, interface or base-class parameter of it, what the body needs of the kinds that reach it: for each call through the parameter, which of the called method's source parameters its result may not point into (the bit [LT-22] records per implementation, read from the kind's table as [LT-48] reads it while running), and which view parameters of the function are used after that call ([BRW-21]). A call from another package checks each kind it gives against that record, followed through its names and calls as within one package, and refuses the call with the same message, naming the library's line (`E3021`: \"`xs` changes while `r` may still look at it (`lib/show.em:9`): `p` is a `Yours`, whose `pick` gives back the list it was handed\"). A kind known only while running is `E3021` with the `runtime` help, as within one package."
findings.codes: E3021 reused; the interface file of [EFF-4] gains the per-`dyn`-parameter record

findings.title: A `thread_shared` value placed in a frame ([OPT-1]) or made `using` a manager has no chunk header to say which thread made it (extends O8)
findings.why: [OPT-1]: "When escape analysis proves that no owner, link or view of an object, a `weakref` link included, outlives the function that made it, the compiler MAY place the object in the function's frame with the same header": a scoped task's owner does not outlive the function, so the condition holds. [OBJ-1]/[RC-4]: "Which thread made a value is read from the header of the memory chunk its block came from, written once when the chunk is made, never from the value", and [OBJ-4] lets a class name a manager with `using`, whose memory ([ALC-1]) carries no such header. Neither rule excludes a `thread_shared` value, and nothing in Part IX does (no rule pairs `thread_shared` with `using`). O8 asks the chunk to keep its thread for the process's life; this is the case of a block that came from no chunk.
findings.proposed_text: Add to [OPT-1]: "A `thread_shared` value is never placed in a frame: its making thread is read from its chunk ([RC-4]), which a frame has not." Add to [OBJ-4]: "A `thread_shared` value's block always comes from the runtime allocator's chunks ([RT-1]), whatever manager its class names: `thread_shared` before a value made `using m` is `E2114` (\"a `thread_shared` value's block carries its making thread's record, which only the runtime allocator keeps; remove `using m`: `names = thread_shared Names()`\")."
findings.codes: E2114 reused (a word that cannot apply to its value), or a sibling if the registry prefers one per word

findings.title: The deferred-drop region's edges are unsaid: early exits, a `yield` inside it, links made by callees, a link that leaves the region
findings.program:
Implementer questions, each forced by one program:
1. fn find(this) -> Option[weakref Node]:
       up = weakref this.leaf
       while up exists as n:
           if n.parent exists as p:
               up = weakref p              # inside the region: holds no weak count
               this.on_visit(p)
               if p.tag == 7: return Some(up)   # <- the link leaves the region holding no count: is the region ended here (the counter decremented, the waiting blocks freed) and the count given to `up` first?
           else: break
2. gen fn walk(this) -> Generator[int]: the same loop with `yield n.tag` inside it: the region stays open while the caller runs anything, so every end on this thread waits for a generator that may never resume.
3. fn drop() of a class that the visit function ends: inside it `w = weakref this.parent` is made while the region is open: is it "a link that lives only inside the region" (no count) or not (it is in another function)?
findings.why: [WK-18]: "the walk is placed in a deferred-drop region ... only their blocks' memory waits, and is freed when the walk ends (one add and one subtract of a per-thread counter per region, nothing per step). A link that lives only inside the region and is given only objects that live at that moment ... holds no weak count": "when the walk ends" names no exits, "lives only inside the region" names no test for a link handed out of it, and a per-thread counter makes every function called from the walk, `drop` bodies included, run inside the region without saying whether their links count. A region left open across a `yield` ([CORO-*]) defers every end on the thread for as long as the generator is paused.
findings.proposed_text: Add to [WK-18]: "The region is the walk's own lines, from the line that makes its first link to every exit of the loop (its end, a `break`, a `return`, a `?`), at each of which the per-thread counter is subtracted and the waiting blocks freed; a walk whose loop holds a `yield` is placed in no region. Only a link made by those lines holds no count; a link made in a function the walk calls, a `drop` included, counts as anywhere. A link made inside the region that leaves it (returned, stored in a place that outlives the walk, handed to a call that keeps it) is given its count at the line that moves it out, one add, before the region ends."

findings.title: "different classes" as proof that two paths differ must exclude a base and its derived class
findings.program:
class Entity: hp: int = 0
class Player(Entity): pass
fn hit(ref mut e: Entity, p: shares mut Player):   # `e` may be `p`'s object: both lead to one class family
    p.hp -= 1                                      # read literally, "different classes" (Entity, Player) proves them apart; E3022 is not raised
findings.why: [EXC-3]: "Two paths may reach the same object when they lead to objects of one class family ... unless the compiler knows they differ: different classes, a fresh object, or the line inside `if a is not b:`". `Entity` and `Player` are different classes of one family, and an `Entity`-typed path may hold a `Player`. findings.proposed_text: In [EXC-3] replace "different classes" with "classes of which neither is the other nor derives from it", and in [BRW-17] "different types" with "types of which neither can hold a value of the other (for classes, neither derives from the other)".

findings.title: `= ref mut` on a `ref mut` parameter writes the caller's place for a view type but re-points the parameter for any other type, and no sentence says which decides
findings.why: [BRW-14]: "a `ref mut dst: MutSpan[float]` parameter given another span points the caller's `d` at it, and `ref mut c: Counter` given another ref points `c`, for the rest of the call, at that place". findings.proposed_text: Add to [BRW-14]: "Which of the two a `ref mut` parameter does is decided by its type: where the type is a view (`ref T`, `ref mut T`, `MutSpan[T]`, `Span[T]`, `StrView`, a view struct), the caller's place holds a view and `= ref mut` writes that view into it ([LT-47] says what may be put there); where it is not, `= ref mut` points the parameter at another place for the rest of the call and the caller's place is untouched."

findings.title: `shares this` outside `drop`, and `shares p` of a parameter whose type is already shared, are decided by no sentence

verdicts.reason: Two of the three questions the text answers. The exemption is static and local: "A link that lives only inside the region and is given only objects that live at that moment (`up = weakref p` from the view `p`) then holds no weak count" with [WK-11]'s "Every `weakref` link holds one weak count on its target ... ([WK-18] gives the one place a proved region keeps the block instead)": a link returned or stored does not "live only inside the region", so it is compiled as [WK-11] says, with its count from its making, and no add is owed at an exit; a link made in a callee (a `drop` included) is compiled by a function that is in no region, so it too holds its count. "freed when the walk ends" with "one add and one subtract of a per-thread counter per region" leaves the subtract at each exit of the loop as the only reading. What is real: a walk whose loop holds a `yield` ([CORO-14] makes a generator a walk) keeps the per-thread counter raised while the generator is paused, so every block freed on the thread waits for a frame that may never resume, and [CORO-7] drops only locals when a suspended generator ends, not the region's counter: the region is never closed.
verdicts.narrowed_to: [WK-18] must exclude a walk whose loop holds a `yield` from the deferred-drop region (or close the region at each `yield` and reopen at the resume), and should state the region's extent (the loop's lines, closed at every exit) and that only links of the walk's own function qualify.
verdicts.better_fix: Add to [WK-18]: "The region is the walk's loop: the counter is added before its first line and subtracted at each exit of the loop (its end, a `break`, a `return`, a `?`); a loop with a `yield` in it is placed in no region, since a suspended generator may never resume ([CORO-13]). Only a link made and ended inside the loop's own lines holds no count; a link that leaves the loop (returned, stored, handed to a call that keeps it), and every link a function the walk calls makes, a `drop` included, holds its count as [WK-11] says."
